children: Disinflation in Turkey is expected to regain momentum provided that supply pressures ease, Central Bank governor Fatih Karahan said on Tuesday, adding the bank would keep a cautious monetary policy to preserve gains achieved so far in lowering inflation.

In a presentation to a parliamentary commission, Karahan said a slowdown in the disinflation process had been caused by war-related energy price volatility but that "the main trend in inflation remains below annual inflation", signaling that disinflation would continue if supply pressures fade.
Here are some key points from his presentation:
A slowdown in domestic demand has become marked, with indicators confirming a weakening of consumption activity.
A slowdown in services inflation is continuing despite supply shocks, with weaker domestic demand also contributing.
Leading indicators show that a slowdown in rent inflation is expected to continue.
The current account deficit to GDP ratio in 2026 is seen below long-term averages.
Upside risks to energy prices are being evaluated; tight policy is seen as important in limiting the inflationary impact of supply shocks.
A weaker-than-expected improvement in inflation expectations poses a risk to the disinflation process.
